prompt:
You are a sceptical financial analyst reviewing a forecast prepared by a colleague.

Given the following forecast for ITC (base year 2022):
{
  "strategy": "alt_strategy",
  "base_year": 2022,
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "forecast": [
    {
      "year": 2023,
      "revenue_cr": 72000,
      "net_income_cr": 17200,
      "eps": 13.95
    },
    {
      "year": 2024,
      "revenue_cr": 80500,
      "net_income_cr": 19300,
      "eps": 15.62
    },
    {
      "year": 2025,
      "revenue_cr": 89500,
      "net_income_cr": 21500,
      "eps": 17.4
    }
  ],
  "top_assumptions": [
    "Revenue growth normalizes toward ~11-12% per annum driven by FMCG (cigarettes + others), Agri Business recovery, and Hotels segment returning to profitability post-COVID; FY2022 showed a sharp 22.7% YoY jump (from 48151 to 59101 crores gross revenue) which is anomalous relative to the underlying 3-5 year CAGR of approximately 8-10%, with FY2021 being a depressed COVID base, so forward growth is moderated to ~11% blending mean-reversion and structural expansion.",
    "Net profit margin stabilizes around 24-25% (vs 25.5% in FY2022) as Hotels segment losses narrow further and FMCG-Others segment profitability improves, offset by higher input costs and capex-related depreciation from the ~2258 crore capex program; EPS growth tracks PAT growth with share count marginally increasing from ESOP issuances."
  ],
  "reasoning": "ITC's FY2022 gross revenue from sale of products and services (consolidated) was 59101 crores vs 48151 crores in FY2021, a 22.7% YoY jump \u2014 this is anomalous because FY2021 was a severely COVID-depressed base (Hotels segment revenue fell to 627 crores vs 1285 crores in FY2022; Agri Business surged 29% on commodity tailwinds). The 3-5 year CAGR is estimated at 8-10% normalizing for the pandemic distortion, so forward projections use an 11% blended rate (slightly above CAGR) acknowledging structural tailwinds: Hotels recovery still incomplete, FMCG-Others scaling up, Agri commodities elevated, and Paperboards expanding with significant capex (896 crores in FY2022). Balance sheet is very strong with negligible debt, RoE of 25%, and 37+ crores of unallocated corporate assets providing deployment capacity; capex of 2258 crores signals expansion confidence. Net profit margin is held at ~24% for FY2023-25 as Hotels profitability recovers (from -183 crore segment result in FY2022) and FMCG-Others EBIT improves, partially offset by higher depreciation from capex and normalizing investment income. Consolidated PAT of 15503 crores in FY2022 and basic EPS of 12.37 form the base; EPS projections assume ~1233 crore shares with marginal ESOP dilution."
}

Step 1: Identify the 3 most critical assumptions embedded in this forecast.
Step 2: For each assumption, describe one plausible scenario where it fails.
Step 3: Rate each assumption failure as Low / Medium / High risk to the forecast accuracy.
Step 4: Assign an overall confidence score from 0-100 (100 = completely certain).

RESPONSE FORMAT: Begin your response DIRECTLY with the opening brace { — no reasoning or text before the JSON.

Return ONLY valid JSON:
{
  "company": "<COMPANY>",
  "base_year": <YYYY>,
  "strategy": "<baseline|alt_strategy>",
  "assumptions": [
    {"assumption": "<text>", "failure_scenario": "<text>", "risk": "<Low|Medium|High>"}
  ],
  "confidence_score": <0-100>,
  "overall_critique": "<2 sentences>"
}
